common_name: Geisha Girl Duranta (Weeping Bicolor Golden Dewdrop)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring after frost danger has passed; Geisha Girl's graceful weeping branches benefit from an open site with room to arch and cascade rather than being crowded by neighboring shrubs.

directions: Geisha Girl is a distinctive weeping selection of golden dewdrop, its long pendulous branches terminating in dense, drooping racemes of deep purple-blue flowers edged in white that give each bloom a bicolor, ruffled appearance quite unlike the solid lavender flowers of the species. The scrambling, fountain-like habit makes it effective as a specimen, informal hedge, or trained standard, and the long flowering racemes are followed by strings of orange-yellow berries that extend seasonal interest into winter. In zone 9 it is usually cut to the ground by hard freezes but resprouts vigorously from the roots each spring, quickly rebuilding its weeping form and flowering by midsummer. Prune lightly after main flushes to encourage branching without shearing away the pendulous racemes that give this cultivar its character.
sources: Queensland Government Department of Agriculture and Fisheries
